tldr: Page 72 presents diverse survey responses from Oregon residents and business organizations on economic competitiveness. Dominant themes include: high tax burden and property tax increases limiting affordability; regulatory and permitting delays constraining business growth; workforce challenges (childcare costs, apprenticeship access, low wages); housing affordability crisis; manufacturing and energy sectors concerned about Climate Protection Program competitiveness; labor advocates emphasizing prevailing wages and worker protections; rural infrastructure gaps outside I-5 corridor.

bullets.text: Respondent notes property tax increases of 3% annually while personal income stagnates, straining affordability
ENTEK International LLC (Lebanon battery separator manufacturer) employs approximately 500 people and contributes less than 1% of statewide EITE emissions
Multiple respondents advocate streamlining permitting and regulatory processes, particularly land use and development approvals
Childcare affordability and availability cited as critical barrier to workforce attraction and retention across industries
Prevailing wage standards and union apprenticeship programs cited as essential models for family-wage jobs and worker prosperity
Manufacturing and energy businesses cite Climate Protection Program as competitive disadvantage relative to other U.S. states
Measure 5/50 property tax reform requested to align Oregon taxes with actual property values
CoEnergy Propane generates approximately $10 million annual revenue but pays more than $250,000 annually in Oregon taxes and fees
Cherriots transit authority announced .7% payroll tax while Oregon currently has .01% statewide payroll tax
Rural infrastructure investment outside I-5 corridor and shovel-ready site development identified as critical needs

bureaus: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries
